definition: The two user-facing latency metrics: how long until output starts (dominated by prefill and queueing) and how fast it streams (dominated by decode).
details: The two user-facing latency metrics: how long until output starts (dominated by prefill and queueing) and how fast it streams (dominated by decode). Interactive products live and die by TTFT; batch pipelines care about total throughput.

explainer.lead: Time to First Token measures how long until output starts, dominated by prefill and queueing, alongside how fast it streams, dominated by decode. These are the two user-facing latency metrics for language models.

tiers.eli5: It is the wait before a reply starts appearing, separate from how quickly the rest of the reply streams in.
tiers.practitioner: Engineers tune prefill and queueing to cut the wait and watch decode speed for streaming quality. A common pitfall is optimising total throughput while the first-token wait stays long for users.
tiers.paperLevel: Formally, it is the elapsed time from request arrival to the first generated token, plus the subsequent rate of token emission. Limits: the two metrics trade off against each other, so a single latency number hides user experience.

explainer.example: In a chat interface, a long pause before the first word appears is a high TTFT, even if the rest of the answer then streams quickly.
